steps.intent: Open the reply composer with the Reply link
Write an AI-generated reply tailored to the email into the Message Body (the recorded text is only an example)
Wait for the reply to auto-save as a draft ('Draft saved' notice); never press Send
Return to the inbox via 'Back to Inbox' and repeat for the next unread email

dataFlow.field: sender name / email content used to write the reply

successCriteria: After opening a row, the message view shows h2.hP subject and the Reply link
After clicking Reply, a contenteditable [aria-label="Message Body"] textbox appears
After typing, the toast 'Draft saved' becomes visible
The Drafts counter (#dcount) increases by one for each processed email
No Send button is ever clicked; each email remains unsent
consequentialActions: Send email (Send button in the reply composer) — STOP-BEFORE: the user only saved a draft, so the widget must never press Send

strategyHints.reason: Opening an email is a client-side row click with no network calls recorded
Subject, sender and body are read from the rendered message view
Reply link click reveals the composer client-side; no network observed
Text must be entered into a contenteditable textbox with input events so autosave triggers
Draft save is confirmed only via the 'Draft saved' toast and #dcount; no network request recorded
Back to Inbox is a client-side button

openQuestions: Should the widget process all unread emails or only the newest N?
What tone or length should the AI-written replies have, and should they be signed with a name?
